decision_basis: User-authorized adjudication after independent controlled HTTP reproduction; no change to the frozen generation or validation run.
business_rule: A user contributes at most one like to a transaction.
decision_text: Associate the candidate with confirmed defect D9: the same user can persist two distinct likes for one transaction. Three independent treatment rounds each returned HTTP 200 twice and stored 0, then 1, then 2 likes; three separately reset two-user controls stored exactly one like per user. The criterion is duplicate persisted records, not the status code alone.

initial_classification.note: The candidate assumes a second like on the same transaction is rejected and likes stays unchanged; in fact the second POST /likes returns 200 and appends a second like record (createLikes in the source code has no de-duplication). This is a lead that a duplicate like is not rejected; it counts as a real defect only after being reproduced separately in a clean environment.
initial_classification.reviewer: author review against the execution evidence (2026-09-12); notes drafted with AI assistance and confirmed by the authors

preserved_records: The original 57-candidate and 37-candidate reviews, initial classifications, M12 evidence and verdicts, generated test suites and prior D8 adjudication are unchanged.
